answer: Meadow 200 plots, each crossed by a drainage ditch. An agent builds a timber footbridge: 12 planks at $4 each; its knot-and-grain pattern is registered once, never reused. Each epoch the agent photographs the same bridge with GPS and timestamp before the dew dries at 09:00; the ledger rejects any photo whose grain matches another bridge or whose dew is gone. Each bridge costs $48 of timber, $60 of labor, $25 a trip. Faking 1,000 identities means building 1,000 real bridges: $133,000 per epoch. A bridge holds only if someone walked its planks; this meadow trusts only feet that crossed.
